title: Scheduled jobs and observability
goal: Design a repeatable background job with observable state and safe cancellation.
prerequisites: onec.p10; P1–P3; explicit contracts, types, collections and failure handling.
outcomes: Actual input/output and exact own source identified; unperformed stages marked NOT RUN.
Accepted original preserved; rejection and its limits explained.
sections: Scheduled jobs trigger procedures; background execution has its own lifecycle and errors. Define input, batch, commit boundary and state. “Every minute” does not mean the prior cycle finished. Prevent overlap by key or handle it through an idempotent design.

The complete runnable fragment is a manual batch-boundary handler, not a scheduled server job. For 12 items/batch5 it yields 5, 10, 12 and remains 12 at completion. Pass position explicitly so future persisted progress can survive calls independently of a form.

Use bounded batches with explicit progress and a persisted continuation point. One long transaction over all history blocks others and complicates recovery. Commit the continuation point with batch results. After failure, retries must neither skip unfinished items nor duplicate accepted ones.

ОдинПакет validates numeric integer inputs, nonnegative position and size≥1. Zero size could otherwise loop without progress. This function neither reads the course nor creates accounts or Nexus background jobs.

Distinguishqueued/running/succeeded/failed/cancelled. A processed counter is not committed success. Check cancellation between safe batches; it does not roll back already committed work. LogjobID, stage, counters and safe error details rather than secrets or full exchange copies.

Append the source to a server module and run ОпытРучногоОбработчика normally. Two assertions check boundaries and zero-size rejection. In another copy add a synthetic operationId/position/status/reason log without document contents or secrets.

File and server deployments have different job behavior; training limits may prevent the exercise. Test normal batches, mid-batch failure, retry, overlap and cancellation in a permitted stand. Manually invoking a function tests its algorithm, not actual scheduled execution. Record those evidence separately.

Actual scheduling needs a supported licensed environment, own job metadata and an observed scheduled start. On a single-user training edition use the manual path and mark scheduling NOT RUN. Closing UI does not cancel an accepted server batch; cancellation needs a separate tested policy.
